rows.name: pyinfra
rows.reason: Reusable Python deployments upload files and run SSH commands with visible output. Arbitrary commands need appropriate repeat-run behavior; files.put documentation cautions against large-file use.

rows.name: Dagu
rows.reason: Ordered transfer/SSH workflow retains output with optional web UI. Requires configured instance/workflow; exact inputs and older-release compatibility unverified. Current main-branch documentation cannot prove June 2026 availability.

rows.name: SSHKit
rows.reason: SSHKit provides Ruby recursive uploads, remote commands, output capture and logging over SSH. Workflow code remains required; command context, quoting and failure behavior need deliberate handling.

rows.name: GitHub-hosted runner
rows.reason: Hosted jobs can run the transfer and command sequence with workflow logs, provided the home lab is reachable through configured networking such as WireGuard.

rows.name: Woodpecker CI
rows.reason: Clones source and runs ordered command steps with pipeline output; SSH/SCP deployment commands can target the lab when the execution agent has network access.

rows.name: Rundeck file-copier and node-executor workflow
rows.reason: Rundeck transfers scripts, executes them through SSH node executors and streams results. This is not complete source-tree deployment; packaging or synchronization must be supplied as a job step.

rows.name: Fabric
rows.reason: Reusable Python tasks upload via SSH and display/capture remote output. Tasks need authoring/maintenance; persistent history, scheduling and a web interface require additional components.

rows.name: Ansible
rows.reason: Ansible copies source and runs remote commands. Inspected shell uses /bin/sh; Windows modules are unverified. Display stdout/stderr deliberately; controller task logging is not ongoing application service logging.

rows.name: pyinfra
rows.reason: Python directory-sync/command workflow requires inventory and commands. server.shell always runs, non-idempotently; default sh requires configuration for alternatives. Choose deletion behavior explicitly; no persistent log dashboard inferred.

rows.name: GitHub-hosted runner
rows.reason: GitHub-hosted runners clone/run/log on GitHub machines. Lab deployment needs explicit transfer/SSH and reachability; target access remains unresolved. Hosted execution is not forbidden and alone does not justify exclusion.

rows.name: Woodpecker CI
rows.reason: Woodpecker CI checks out source and runs upload/SSH steps with logs. Requires transfer tools, credentials and lab connectivity; container-only builds do not supply the requested remote execution.

rows.name: Woodpecker email outreach
rows.reason: woodpecker.co is email/LinkedIn prospecting and campaigns, operating on leads and outreach rather than transferring source code and executing lab-machine commands. Its shared name does not identify Woodpecker CI.

rows.name: Woodpecker email outreach
rows.reason: This product automates prospecting, email and LinkedIn outreach, so its documented capabilities do not address source transfer, remote command execution or deployment logs.

rows.name: Ansible copy and script modules
rows.reason: Ansible copy/script can transfer source and execute local scripts remotely. SSH script execution merges stderr into stdout; use copy plus command when separate streams are needed.

rows.name: Semaphore UI
rows.reason: Semaphore UI provides Git-backed automation with reusable web tasks and per-run status/logs. Requires service hosting, execution tools, repository access, credentials and actual deployment steps.

rows.name: Fabric
rows.reason: Fabric provides Python upload/run tasks and visible output. Write deployment steps; put documents file upload, not recursive trees. Archive/extraction is custom mapping; persistent application-log collection remains unestablished.

rows.name: Dokku
rows.reason: Git-push pipeline builds/deploys applications and exposes logs, replacing manual copying. Requires adopting Dokku's application model; durable old-deployment history needs external persistence.
